posts.title: Autumn term timetable published
posts.excerpt: Day and evening schedules are final for the term beginning 14 September.
posts.content:
Day and evening schedules are now final for the Autumn term beginning 14 September. Day classes meet Monday and Wednesday 09:30–15:30; evening classes meet Tuesday and Thursday 18:30–21:00.

Each paper is 36 class hours across the twelve weeks. The mock papers fall in week 6 (practice) and week 9 (full mock); week 12 is exam week, and results follow six weeks later.

Groups are limited to sixteen learners and fill in order of registration. To book a placement chat, call +1 555 0142 or visit the college office at 14 Corder Street.

posts.title: What the Mock Paper Day Is Like
posts.excerpt: Every term at Kanjo College, week nine brings daytime and evening students together for a timed, full-length simulation of official examination conditions.
posts.content:
At Kanjo College, week nine of every twelve-week term is marked on the calendar for a specific reason: the full mock paper day. Introduced across our curriculum in 2021, this dedicated Saturday sitting brings together daytime and evening students at 14 Corder Street to experience full examination conditions before sitting their official papers. While week six includes an informal classroom practice exercise, week nine is deliberately structured to mirror external examination rules in every detail, providing adult learners with an authentic assessment trial.

The day begins at our Northgate campus well before desks are occupied. Samuel Kwan, who manages the exams office and has supervised assessment sessions for ten years, oversees the preparation of the examination rooms. Desks are spaced according to formal examination distance regulations, equipped only with printed question papers, blank ruled ledger answer sheets, and standard reference materials. Learners arrive from 08:30 onwards, register at reception, and store their bags and mobile phones in lockers before taking their allocated seats.

For working adults, the greatest challenge of an accounting examination is rarely mathematical ability alone; it is the discipline of managing time under silence. During ordinary evening classes on Tuesday and Thursday or daytime sessions on Monday and Wednesday, students frequently discuss adjustments with lecturers or consult their notes. On mock paper day, the room falls completely silent once Samuel Kwan announces the start. Over the three-hour timed session, students must interpret transactional data, prepare journal entries, balance ledger columns, and resolve complex tax or variance questions entirely from memory.

Candidates sit mocks across all four subjects taught at the college: Financial Accounting, Management Accounting, Tax and Payroll, and Audit and Assurance. While enrolled students take the assessment as part of their standard term tuition—which covers thirty-six class hours alongside all examination preparation—the mock paper day is also open to independent external students for a stand-alone fee of $85. These external candidates join our cohorts in Northgate to test their preparation against rigorous, independently marked standards.

Once the allotted time ends and papers are collected, the atmosphere transitions from silent concentration to collective analysis. Rather than leaving students waiting weeks for diagnostic information, our teaching faculty—including Tomás Ferreira, Grace Okonjo, Pieter van Dalen, and Amira Haddad—review the scripts with detailed handwritten feedback. Marked papers are returned individually during week ten, accompanied by precise notes on layout errors, omitted workings, or calculation slips that could cost critical marks. Principal Helena Marsh often notes that the primary benefit of the mock sitting is identifying procedural blind spots early, while there is still ample classroom time to correct them.

By demystifying examination day protocols well ahead of week twelve, the mock paper day replaces anxiety with methodical routine. Students leave 14 Corder Street knowing exactly how to budget their minutes across complex calculations, how to format ledger balance sheets cleanly under time pressure, and how to approach official professional assessments with quiet, earned composure. With results from official exam sessions published six weeks after week twelve, learners who complete our rigorous mock process enter their final assessments with tested endurance, familiar timing habits, and dependable confidence in their bookkeeping technique.

posts.title: Evening library hours extended
posts.excerpt: Study rooms and library desks now stay open until 20:30 on weekdays.
posts.content:
Study rooms and library desks now stay open until 20:30 on weekdays, so learners can review ledger exercises after work or before an evening class.

The rooms at 14 Corder Street open with the college office: Monday to Friday until 20:30, Saturday until 13:00, and closed on Sunday.

The study rooms are quiet by rule. Small-group work happens in the classrooms before evening classes begin at 18:30.
